question.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1+2t+3{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=-3-t-2{t}^{3}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =3\cdot (1+2t+3{t}^{2})+(-1)\cdot (-3-t-2{t}^{3}) \\  & =3+6t+9{t}^{2}-(-3-t-2{t}^{3}) \\  & =6+7t+9{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
